chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with a woman and kissed her, other than the fact that he had not ejaculated into her, then he married her daughter. He said: If he had not ejaculated into the mother, there is no harm (in marrying the daughter), and if he had ejaculated, he should not marry her.

key_terms.بَاشَرَ: To have sexual intercourse or engage in conjugal relations
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does a man who had intercourse with a woman but did not ejaculate become prohibited from marrying her daughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the condition of *khalw* (seclusion) and consummation in establishing the prohibition of marrying a stepdaughter, distinguishing between mere intercourse and full consummation with ejaculation. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores that the barrier to marriage is the actual consummation (*khalw biha*) rather than just the act of penetration, reflecting the principle that the mother and daughter become sisters in marriage only upon complete union. This distinction is crucial for understanding the nuances of *mahram* relationships derived from marriage.
